answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may vote on tasks or claim rewards. A newcomer can create a thousand keys, but each key needs its own deposit; identities caught coordinating fake work lose stake, while honest agents recover it after a delay. This makes a Sybil attack costly in capital and exposes the attacker to losses, rather than treating account creation itself as proof of personhood. The voyage from dawn to nectar is cheap in a story, but not when every alias must put money at risk.
